title: Watchdog-recovery-spawn architecture gap -- pause guards stop new spawns, in-flight orphans run SKILL to completion
decision: Surface a system property exposed by the 12:44-17:57Z timeline on 2026-05-23. The three pause guards in current operation -- `scripts/cron_paused.flag`, MCP-side `aig-mode1-sprint enabled=false`, and the watchdog's flag-aware short-circuit (per entry 17, 2026-05-22T18:33:47Z) -- collectively stop NEW spawns: cron will not fire, MCP will not trigger, the watchdog will not initiate fresh crash-recovery workers. They do NOT stop already-spawned headless `claude -p` recovery workers from running their SKILL.md to completion. Once a recovery worker has been launched (typically a 10-15 min headless run), no in-process signal currently exists to interrupt it short of force-killing the PID tree. The companion WCK finalization entry above is one concrete instance of this gap. Overnight stability evidence (2026-05-23 evening through 2026-05-24 morning): a 16-PID claude-code-related process pile was identified at session start. 11 of those were Claude Desktop processes (left alive, not orphans). 7 were CC workers, killed individually with per-PID verification (none respawned). Process count went 16 -> 9 and held at 9 with zero respawn. Watchdog log showed continuous skip-paused entries from 13:07Z through this morning's 06:02Z with zero crash-confirm triggers. Zero new sprint commits, zero new sentinel touches, zero new Telegram messages were generated between 17:57Z and reaping time. This bounds the gap as ONE-SHOT -- orphans exit cleanly after SKILL completion, they do not persist as daemons and do not re-spawn. Risk window per orphan = one SKILL execution (~10-15 min); risk window per pause incident = (orphans spawned during the kill-burst) * (orphan SKILL duration).
rationale: Naming a system property is the precondition for closing it. The 2026-05-22T18:33:47Z fix added `cron_paused.flag` as a watchdog signal but framed pause as 'stop new fires'. The WCK orphan-spawn revealed that 'in-flight workers' is a third category alongside cron-driven fires and watchdog-driven recoveries. Recording the gap as ONE-SHOT is load-bearing -- it means future pause incidents do not require unbounded vigilance, they require a finite drain wait. Cowork reading the audit chain should see this gap stated explicitly, not inferred from a sequence of incident entries. alternatives_considered: Defer documenting until a remediation is implemented (rejected -- audit chain self-correctness requires the gap be visible BEFORE the fix lands so Cowork sees the system honestly)

title: Append to entry 24 (2026-05-23T13:20:16Z) -- catch-up cap x iteration budget exceeds stale threshold by design
decision: Add to entry 24's analysis the explicit arithmetic that makes the SKILL gap binding regardless of agent discretion. Catch-up cap = 4 iterations; per-iteration sprint budget = ~10 min; max catch-up window = 4 x 10 = ~40 min. Watchdog stale-sentinel threshold = 30 min. 40 > 30 by 33%. A fully-utilizing cap-bound catch-up burst will exceed the stale threshold even if every iteration is healthy and progressing. Entry 24 framed the missing `--mark-done` as 'agent discretion' (sprint_catchup.py:247 docstring leaves the question to the agent); this entry sharpens that to: agent discretion CANNOT resolve the timing conflict -- the budget math forecloses any safe choice that does not refresh the sentinel mid-burst. Therefore the SKILL.md patch in Task C is necessary, not optional. Without explicit `sprint_catchup.py --mark-done` between iterations, the SKILL race-loses to the watchdog by design on long catch-up windows.
rationale: Entry 24 documents the WHAT (sprint killed because sentinel went stale during burst); this entry documents the WHY in arithmetic the next reader can verify without re-deriving. Existence-proof analysis ('one incident occurred') is weaker evidence for patch necessity than design-proof analysis ('math forecloses any non-patching choice'). Cowork reading the chain would see entry 24 say 'agent did not refresh sentinel between iterations' and could reasonably ask 'why didn't the agent just refresh?'. This entry answers: the agent COULD have refreshed; the patch makes that the default instead of leaving it as discretion. Both entries together close the question.

Skip the entry and put the math only into the SKILL.md patch commit message (rejected -- the decision log is the canonical Cowork audit surface; commit messages are downstream documentation, not primary audit chain)

title: SKILL.md patched -- per-iteration sprint_catchup.py --mark-done; catch-up sentinel-stale bug closed; no-housekeeping execution path remains deferred
decision: This entry records the SKILL.md patch applied 2026-05-24 to close the cron-triggered catch-up burst sentinel-stale bug captured in entry 24 (`2026-05-23T13:20:16Z`, commit c92d080) and analyzed arithmetically in entry 27 (commit 22792bc). **Patch.** Modifies the iteration-structure prose in step 1 of `C:\Users\ahmed\.claude\scheduled-tasks\aig-mode1-sprint\SKILL.md`. Adds explicit loop wrapping (`Run steps 2-5 below min(N, 4) + 1 times total`) and inserts a sentinel-refresh call (`python scripts/sprint_catchup.py --mark-done`) at the START of each iteration body, including iteration 1. Also disambiguates the prior `Cap at 4 iterations/fire` line to `Cap at 4 catch-up iterations + 1 current = 5 total sprint cycles per fire` matching entry 24's framing. Includes inline rationale referencing entries 24 and 27 so future readers of SKILL.md see both the what (call --mark-done per iteration) and the why (cap times budget exceeds stale-threshold without refresh). **Scope: CRON-TRIGGERED CATCH-UP BURST SENTINEL-STALE BUG ONLY.** Without per-iteration sentinel refresh, the 4-iter cap times ~10-min budget reaches ~50 min and exceeds the watchdog's 30-min stale-sentinel threshold, causing the watchdog to kill the running sprint burst mid-iteration (as observed `2026-05-23T12:44:42Z`). With per-iteration refresh at iteration START, the watchdog sees stale age <= one iteration runtime (~10 min) and will not fire spuriously during the burst. Start-of-iteration placement (rather than end-of-iteration) is the monotonically safer choice: if the sentinel was already ~25 min stale at fire entry, a 10-min iteration ending at 35 min stale would trigger the watchdog mid-iteration -- start-of-iteration refresh eliminates that vulnerability. **Scope: this patch does NOT address the no-housekeeping execution path** used by watchdog-recovery-spawned workers. That category-level finding -- the three sprint commits on 2026-05-23 (c6dec3d, 97cdf93, 687fd7e) share a no-sentinel-touch / no-Telegram / no-missed_sprints-update fingerprint -- is a separate bug class deferred to a future fresh-budget session per entry 28's `alternatives_considered` item 4. The deferred investigation requires reads of `scripts/session_resume_prompt.txt`, the sprint_catchup.py SKILL preamble path, and the watchdog's exact spawn command in `scripts/cc_watchdog.ps1`. **Both fixes needed for full coverage.** This patch covers normal cron-fired sprints; the deferred investigation covers watchdog-recovery-spawned workers. Until the second fix lands, orphan-spawn artifacts may still produce sprint commits without proper housekeeping touches. **SKILL.md location.** Outside the aig_engine git repo at user-scoped `C:\Users\ahmed\.claude\scheduled-tasks\aig-mode1-sprint\SKILL.md` per Claude Code's scheduling-system design (see entry 22). The SKILL.md edit therefore produces no git artifact; this decision_log entry IS the audit-chain record of the patch. Re-unpause sequencing (cron_paused.flag removal + MCP enable=true) is deferred to a separate session with explicit checkpoints -- the cron-paused state from 2026-05-23T13:07Z remains in effect. **Verification step queued for the re-unpause session (not this one):** confirm Claude Code reads SKILL.md fresh on each cron fire vs caching it between fires. The simplest check after applying the SKILL.md edit is to inspect MCP `list_scheduled_tasks` output for `aig-mode1-sprint` -- if the description field reflects the updated text, the harness has loaded the new SKILL; if it still shows the old description, a cache may need clearing before re-unpause is safe.
rationale: The audit chain requires a concrete record when a documented bug gets patched, especially when the patched file lives outside the git surface (so the audit chain cannot rely on `git log` to find the change). Without this entry, a future Cowork audit would see entries 24/27/28 documenting the bug + corrections but no record that the bug was actually fixed. Entry 29 closes that loop. The scope-carving language (what the patch does and does not cover) prevents a future reader from assuming the SKILL.md patch is the complete fix -- it is not; orphan-spawn artifacts via the recovery-spawn path are still possible until the deferred investigation lands its own fix.
alternatives_considered: Skip decision_log entry, rely on chat-transcript memory of the patch (rejected -- audit-chain integrity requires a permanent record; chat transcripts are not part of the audit surface and Cowork reads only the git-tracked decision_log)

methodology_source = infrastructure_decision (defensible alternative -- the patch IS an infrastructure/tooling fix; chose audit_finding_resolution because the bug was specifically documented in entries 24/27/28 and this patch closes that documented finding, which fits the enum's intent more tightly; CEO leaned this direction in the approval message)

Commit SKILL.md into the aig_engine repo for direct git tracking (rejected this session -- would require rethinking Claude Code's user-scoped scheduled-tasks design; not in scope for Task C. Could be considered as a future infrastructure decision when the scheduling architecture is revisited)

Apply the patch without writing a decision_log entry (rejected -- inconsistent with the audit-chain discipline that documented the bug; the patch resolution must be recorded in the same surface where the bug was named)

End-of-iteration --mark-done placement instead of start-of-iteration (rejected -- end-of-iteration leaves iteration 1 vulnerable when the sentinel was already stale at fire entry; start-of-iteration is monotonically safer and was confirmed by CEO this session)

title: Correction to entry 29 -- MCP description field reflects SKILL.md frontmatter, not body; entry 29's verification mechanism was structurally flawed
decision: On 2026-05-24 (post-Task-C entry 29 commit, this session), called MCP `list_scheduled_tasks` to perform the cache-verification step queued in entry 29. The returned description field for `aig-mode1-sprint` was: "AIG Phase 1 directive-compliant sprint -- drains existing queue, runs paper-forward detector, regenerates dashboard, commits. No autonomous strategy enrollment. Strategy slots driven by the three-filter methodology in strategy_register.md, not by queue-emptiness." This is byte-identical to the SKILL.md YAML frontmatter `description:` line (a fact already established in entry 23, 'MCP-side description in sync with SKILL.md frontmatter (byte-identical)'). The patch in entry 29 modified the BODY of SKILL.md (the iteration-structure block inside step 1), not the frontmatter. Therefore the MCP description field could never reflect the patched body content, regardless of whether the MCP scheduled-tasks subsystem caches SKILL.md body between fires. The verification mechanism proposed in entry 29 ('inspect MCP list_scheduled_tasks output for aig-mode1-sprint -- if the description field reflects the updated text, the harness has loaded the new SKILL') was structurally unable to verify what it claimed. This is the same class of audit-chain drift as the 33d93ae lesson (entries 21/22): a load-bearing audit-surface claim that does not match the underlying reality. **Authoritative correction.** Any future SKILL.md patch verification that aims to test cache state must either (a) include a frontmatter `description:` bump so the MCP-exposed field changes visibly, (b) restart Claude Code to force MCP runtime cache invalidation, or (c) observe first-fire behavior directly. The MCP description-field-changed criterion alone is insufficient for body-only patches. **What IS verified about the entry 29 patch.** The Edit tool's success message confirms the patch landed on disk in SKILL.md ('The file ... has been updated successfully'). The on-disk SKILL.md file content is the patched version. What remains unverified at the MCP layer is whether the scheduled-tasks subsystem will read that on-disk version at the next fire, or use a stale in-memory cached version. Entry 31 (next entry below, this commit chain) records the operational decision on how to proceed despite the unresolved cache question.
rationale: Same audit-chain self-correction discipline invoked at entries 21/22: when a load-bearing claim in a prior entry turns out to be wrong, the correction is recorded as a new entry rather than by editing the original. Entry 29's verification step was clear enough that a future Cowork audit would have followed it literally and reached a wrong conclusion -- either 'description unchanged, cache OK, proceed' (optimistic misread) or 'description unchanged, cache stale, halt re-unpause indefinitely' (pessimistic misread). Either outcome would be based on a misunderstanding of what the MCP description field actually represents. Naming the flaw explicitly prevents that downstream error.
alternatives_considered: Edit entry 29 in-place to fix the verification step (rejected -- violates append-only discipline established at entries 21/22)

Skip the correction and just proceed with first-fire verification (rejected -- entry 29's verification step would remain a future-audit hazard; correcting it explicitly maintains audit-chain integrity)

Bump SKILL.md frontmatter description as part of this correction so the verification mechanism becomes usable retroactively (deferred -- if a body-only patch verification is needed in the future, the frontmatter-bump pattern can be considered as part of THAT patch's design; not retrofitting entry 29's patch this session)

title: Cron re-enable (Option D) -- accept cache verification uncertainty; use first fire as verification mechanism; accept recovery-spawn architecture gap per entries 26/28
decision: Re-enable cron Cloud Routine `aig-mode1-sprint` after Task C SKILL.md patch landed (entry 29) and the cache-verification mechanism in entry 29 was acknowledged structurally flawed (entry 30 above). **Option D verification path selected.** Use the first cron fire post-unpause as the verification mechanism. **Primary success criterion** (the only observable that uniquely distinguishes 'patched SKILL ran' from 'old SKILL ran'): `last_sprint_fire.txt` advances every ~10 min during the catch-up burst. The per-iteration sentinel touch is the specific behavior the entry 29 patch added; sentinel advancement is the direct observable of patch effect. **Corroborative signals** (confirm but do not uniquely prove): per-iteration `SENTINEL_UPDATED=<ts>` lines in the sprint agent's stdout (confirms the script-level call ran); no new 'CRASH CONFIRMED' entries in `crash_log.md` during the burst window (confirms watchdog did not need to intervene). **Necessary but not sufficient:** a clean sprint commit landing on `origin/main` at burst end. The old SKILL could also produce a commit if the burst happened to complete before the 30-min stale threshold (e.g., if the queue drained faster than expected and the burst exited early). Commit-landing alone does NOT prove the patch is in effect. **Failure criterion (preemptive, ~15-min headroom on watchdog's 30-min stale threshold):** if `last_sprint_fire.txt` has NOT advanced beyond Step 2's manual touch timestamp by ~15 minutes after the first cron fire begins (first-fire start visible via process spawn or first agent output), declare failure preemptively and recreate the flag BEFORE the watchdog stale-check fires. This gives 15-min headroom on the 30-min threshold and aborts the burst while still within the original sentinel's stale-safe window. Without this preemptive check, the failure signal would arrive ~30+ min into the burst (when watchdog fires CRASH CONFIRMED), well into burst execution and harder to abort cleanly. **Failure criterion (late detection, fallback):** sentinel does not advance mid-burst (old SKILL loaded from cache), watchdog fires CRASH CONFIRMED, recovery-spawn loop initiates. **In the failure case:** immediately recreate `scripts/cron_paused.flag` + MCP disable to halt the loop, then proceed to Option A (frontmatter description bump) for the next attempt. **Architectural acceptance.** The recovery-spawn no-housekeeping execution path (documented in entries 26/28/29) remains a known gap. If a recovery-spawn produces a sprint commit during the catch-up burst or subsequent fires (next 24-48 hours), it is accepted as known-pattern; entries will be updated to record it as part of the established gap, not treated as a new bug. **Pause-window context.** Pause established at 2026-05-23T13:07Z (entries 19/20); current pause duration ~22 hours. Cron `12,27,42,57 * * * *` with 347s jitter; ~22 hours / 15-min cadence = ~88 nominal missed fires. Catch-up cap is `min(MISSED_FIRES, 4) + 1` = 5 sprint cycles, each up to 10 min. With the entry 29 patch, each iteration starts by refreshing the sentinel via `python scripts/sprint_catchup.py --mark-done`, so the watchdog-visible stale age is bounded at ~10 min throughout the burst. First fire expected to complete in ~40-50 min wall-clock.
rationale: Path A (genuine new Phase 1 strategies via three-filter methodology, frozen-before-data) requires autonomous sprint cadence to make progress; running sprints manually does not scale. The entry 29 patch closes the documented bug that broke the previous re-unpause (entries 23 -> 24). Option D accepts that the cache-loaded-or-not question is genuinely unresolved (per entry 30) but bounds the failure mode: if cache is stale, the result is the same kill-burst pattern from 2026-05-23, for which we now have an explicit recovery playbook (recreate flag + MCP disable). The watchdog v1.4 daily-cap (entry 18) provides a second-line safeguard. Failure cost: one wasted catch-up burst + one decision_log entry recording the cache-stale finding. Success cost: zero. Asymmetry favors attempting. The criterion restructuring (primary vs corroborative vs necessary-but-not-sufficient) addresses a previously-implicit conflation -- a commit landing is observable but does not uniquely prove patch effect, while sentinel advancement during the burst IS uniquely tied to the patched behavior. The preemptive failure criterion (~15-min sentinel-stale-check from the surveillance session) gives explicit abort headroom on the watchdog's 30-min threshold; without it, failure would only surface when the watchdog already started spawning recovery workers, which is harder to recover from cleanly.
alternatives_considered: Wait for a fresh session and attempt Option A (frontmatter description bump) first (rejected -- adds one more session of cron-paused time during which Phase 1 work cannot progress; the failure mode of Option D is bounded and recoverable in the same session)

Option B -- restart Claude Code to force MCP cache invalidation (deferred -- requires CEO to exit + relaunch CC, operational overhead this session does not have authority to require; held in reserve if Option D fails)

Skip re-unpause until the no-housekeeping execution-path investigation lands (rejected -- the no-housekeeping gap is independent of the cron-triggered path; cron-fired sprints with the entry 29 patch should not trigger the no-housekeeping pattern, only recovery-spawned workers do)

Re-unpause without supervision and accept whatever happens (rejected -- 2026-05-23 demonstrated that unsupervised post-pause cron resumption can produce hours of recovery-loop activity; supervised first-fire is the discipline this session has been building)

Use any-of-four success criteria framing as originally drafted (rejected -- conflates the uniquely-discriminating signal (sentinel advancement) with corroborative or necessary-but-not-sufficient signals; commit-landing alone could occur under either old or patched SKILL, so treating it as a success criterion would create a false-positive risk)

Use only the watchdog CRASH CONFIRMED as the failure signal (rejected -- that signal arrives ~30+ min into the burst, well past the point where clean abort is possible; the preemptive 15-min sentinel-check fires earlier and within the original sentinel's stale-safe window)

title: Framework directive amendment -- per-market strategy caps; TradingView sources permitted with qualification criteria; 12-month coverage target; 6-month freeze broken 2 days in with explicit rationale
decision: Amends the Phase 1 framework directive committed 2026-05-22 (commit 33d93ae, embedded in strategy_register.md lines 41-211). Three substantive changes plus one timeline change. **Change 1 -- Phase 1 strategy cap (amends strategy_register.md lines 119-126).** Original cap of 4 candidates total replaced by per-market caps: US = 6 slots, UAE = 4 slots, Crypto = 3 slots, total 13. Divergence remains as US slot 1 (cleared via Session 5 framework selection, grandfathered, no re-validation required). All other slots (US 2-6, UAE 1-4, Crypto 1-3) are OPEN and require three-filter methodology selection plus validation gate passage to fill. The 12 Pre-Framework strategies (mbv, dbo, roc, vcb, hat, pmr, str, art, cmf, gap, wck, ema200) plus 1 grandfathered (divergence, which fills US slot 1) make up the 13 historical strategies in strategy_register.md lines 237-251. The 12 Pre-Framework strategies do NOT auto-fill any slot under this amendment -- including WCK's PORTFOLIO_CLEARED verdict from 2026-05-23 commit 687fd7e (orphan-spawn pathway, entries 25/28). Pre-Framework strategies may be re-tested under the amended gate per directive Part 3 (Method A fresh OOS or Method B post-2026-05-22 forward data); if a re-test passes, it fills a slot. **Change 2 -- Source priority (amends strategy_register.md lines 167-176 and 178-184).** Original source priority list (Lopez de Prado -> replication -> Tareq constrained) is expanded to include TradingView strategies meeting the following qualification criteria, ALL of which must hold: (A) public backtest visible on TradingView covering at least 5 years of data; (B) backtest run on a recognizable universe (S&P 500, Russell 1000, or equivalent index -- not cherry-picked tickers); (C) code/parameters visible enough to re-implement and pre-register against our own universe before any test against our data; (D) strategy published/visible for at least 6 months (avoid newly-published over-fits). The original Part 4 prohibition on "Scanning Pine forum top-returns lists" (strategy_register.md line 180) is replaced by: "Scanning TradingView strategies permitted ONLY if criteria A+B+C+D all hold." All other prohibitions remain in force unchanged: no parameter optimization across universe (line 181), no iterating on failed strategies (line 182), no CEO scanning past results to spot patterns (line 183), no Ahmed intuitions as inputs except via the Ahmed-input exception (line 184). The Ahmed-input exception (lines 186-191), data reuse policy (lines 193-196), and autonomous-execution scope (lines 198-212) all remain in force unchanged. The three-filter methodology (Filter 1 archetype diversity, Filter 2 evidence tier T1/T2/T3, Filter 3 infrastructure readiness -- lines 131-166) remains in force unchanged and applies to all new slot selection across all three markets. **Change 3 -- Coverage target.** Adds explicit 12-month coverage target: 75% of tickers in each market's shared universe showing winning trades under at least one cleared Phase 1 strategy. Target measured per market (US, UAE, Crypto each independently must hit 75%, not aggregated). Target is aspirational, not a hard deadline -- strategies still must pass the validation gate to count. If only N of 13 slots clear and the remaining slots fail honest tests, coverage stops at N's actual ticker count, not lowered gate to force coverage. **Change 4 -- Freeze acknowledgment.** Original directive (strategy_register.md lines 43-49) declared a 6-month freeze ending ~2026-11-22. This amendment breaks the freeze 2 days into its 6-month window. The break is acknowledged explicitly here rather than left implicit. Rationale: the original directive's goal was establishing the framework as substrate for autonomous Phase 1 operation, which has now landed (SKILL.md patched per entry 29, cron re-enabled per entry 31, first verified autonomous fire confirmed today). The new goal -- 75% ticker coverage across three markets within 12 months -- requires scaffolding the original directive was not designed for (per-market caps, broader source set). Continuing with the original cap of 4 would mean accepting that the new goal is unreachable under the original directive. Amending honestly is more honest than either pretending the original goal still applies or pretending the original directive still holds while violating it. **What is preserved.** Three-filter methodology (unchanged), validation gate (unchanged -- min_expectancy >= 1.0, dSharpe >= 0.5, min trades per universe), pre-registration discipline (unchanged -- config_hash before data), append-only audit chain (unchanged), decision_log infrastructure (entries 23+ per directive Part 7, unchanged), re-validation discipline (unchanged -- Method A/B for Pre-Framework strategies). **What this amendment does NOT change.** The walk-forward research track (entry 33, this commit chain) is a separate parallel effort and is NOT a framework amendment -- it operates outside both the original directive and this amendment under explicit boundary rules captured in entry 33.
rationale: The original directive's cap of 4 strategies plus pure-source restrictions was designed to prevent the survivorship-bias and selection-bias pattern that produced the 13 Pre-Framework strategies. Those prevention mechanisms were correct for the original goal. But the original goal was narrow: establish framework discipline. The current goal -- coverage across markets -- requires more strategies and broader sources without abandoning the prevention mechanisms. The amendment threads this by: (a) raising the cap but applying it per-market (so quality control still applies per market), (b) permitting TradingView as source but with criteria A+B+C+D as the new quality bar replacing 'no scanning at all,' (c) keeping every other prohibition unchanged, (d) keeping the three-filter methodology unchanged so the selection mechanism that survived audit remains the selection mechanism going forward. The amendment is intentionally a *modification* of the directive, not a replacement -- Parts 1 (pause), 2 (improvements), 3 (re-validation discipline), 5 (Mode 1/2), 6 (Telegram), 7 (decision log), 8 (order of operations) all remain in force.
alternatives_considered: Stay within the original directive's cap of 4 (rejected -- math: 4 strategies times typical 20-30% per-market coverage = 60-80% upper bound, but only if strategies are diverse, and only if all 4 clear; expected coverage with realistic clear rates ~50%; this falls short of the 75% target and lying to ourselves about the math is worse than amending)

Raise cap to 8 total without per-market breakdown (rejected -- concentrates risk; if all 8 cleared strategies happen to be US-archetype-fits, UAE and Crypto get 0; per-market caps force diversification)
Raise cap to unlimited (rejected -- reopens the survivorship-bias loop the original directive was built to close; no upper bound on selection = no quality control)

title: Walk-forward research track (Track 3) added as parallel separate effort -- boundary against framework directive (Track 1) and amendment (Track 2)
decision: Establishes a third research track operating in parallel with but separate from the original framework directive (Track 1, strategy_register.md lines 41-212) and the framework amendment per entry 32 (Track 2). **Track 3 -- Walk-forward research on historical data.** Method: pick strategy + ticker + long-history dataset (>=5 years available). Split data into training period (years 1 through N minus 6 months) and held-out test period (last 6 months). Develop or backtest strategy on training period. Evaluate strategy performance on held-out test period. If performance on held-out period is consistent with training period, the hypothesis 'strategy is robust to held-out time windows' is supported (NOT confirmed as paper-forward -- see boundary rules below). If performance diverges, the hypothesis is rejected. **Purpose.** Test the philosophical hypothesis that strategies which perform well on held-out historical windows may also perform well in true forward time. This is a research effort. It is NOT a strategy clearance mechanism. **Boundary rules (the discipline that keeps Track 3 honest):** (1) Telegram signals from Track 3 carry the literal label "WALK-FORWARD RESEARCH SIGNAL -- NOT PAPER-FORWARD VERIFIED" -- operator must see this label every time. (2) Track 3 results live in a separate file (`walk_forward_research.json` or equivalent, to be defined when Track 3 first runs), NOT in `strategy_register.md` or `paper_forward_positions.json`. (3) Track 3 strategies do NOT auto-promote to slot fills in Tracks 1 or 2. If a Track 3 strategy looks promising and operator wants to elevate it to a real slot, it must be re-tested under Tracks 1/2 rules: three-filter methodology selection, full pre-registration, validation gate passage, then paper-forward in real time. Walk-forward verification on historical data alone does NOT count as paper-forward verification. (4) Track 3 cannot consume autonomous loop resources. The cron runs Tracks 1 and 2 work (monitor cleared strategies, regenerate dashboard, paper-forward detector on cleared watchlists). Track 3 work happens exclusively in supervised CC sessions initiated by operator. (5) Track 3 results are NOT cited as evidence in any Track 1 or Track 2 decision_log entry. Walk-forward results are research observations, not directive evidence. **What Track 3 is NOT.** Track 3 is not a backdoor for adding strategies that would fail Track 2's qualification criteria. It is not a way to call held-out backtest results 'paper-forward.' It is not a way to bypass the three-filter methodology. Anyone reading this entry should understand that Track 3 exists to test a specific operator-stated hypothesis under explicitly-labeled research conditions, and the boundary rules above are what prevent it from becoming the survivorship-bias-amplifying mechanism the original framework directive was designed to prevent.
rationale: Operator stated in this session that they hold a hypothesis about whether held-out historical-window backtests predict forward performance. Testing the hypothesis is legitimate research. Pretending the test is 'paper-forward' would be dishonest -- the held-out data already exists and the strategy selection is influenced by knowledge of that data. The boundary rules in this entry are the discipline that lets the test happen honestly: clear labeling, separate storage, no auto-promotion, no consumption of disciplined-track resources. Without those boundaries, Track 3 would slowly contaminate Tracks 1 and 2 by ambiguity (operator's brain treats 'experimental win' the same as 'real win' if labels are weak). With the boundaries, Track 3 is a useful research instrument that informs operator's intuition without compromising the disciplined tracks' integrity.
alternatives_considered: Don't add Track 3; stay disciplined within Tracks 1+2 only (rejected -- operator wants to test the hypothesis; refusing to scaffold the test means operator either runs it informally without audit-chain integration or doesn't run it at all, both worse than scaffolded test with boundaries)

title: Retire 3x/10x annual mandate — replace with Kelly-bound realistic anchor (5-10% CAGR)
decision: Retire the 3x/10x annual return mandate (hard minimum 200%, aspirational 1,000%) as a project target. Replace with a constraint-physics-realistic anchor: portfolio compounding at 5-10% CAGR with sub-1% drawdown, where per-strategy edge is measured by the validation gate and portfolio output is the sized aggregation of cleared strategies. The 5-10% figure is an ANCHOR measured toward, NOT a target chased — the moment it becomes a hard target, the phantom-mandate distortion returns. No mandate above the Kelly bound is accepted.
rationale: Per Kelly-bound derivation: CAGR ≤ (Sharpe²/2) × (risk_used / optimal_Kelly_risk). For AIG's locked 1.5% per-trade risk cap (Rule 8) against a full-Kelly optimum of ~20-30% for daily-frequency strategies, the used fraction is ~5-7.5% of optimal Kelly. This yields a ceiling band of approximately 5-10% CAGR, with 15% requiring a Sharpe of ~2.0 (world-class, near-impossible in retail halal long-only no-leverage markets). The 3x/10x mandate (200-1000% CAGR) would require Sharpe ratios that do not exist in this constraint box. Continued operation under the phantom mandate produces goalpost-relocation pressure on every Track 2 candidate selection. Honest retirement is consistent with the framework directive's Brutal Honesty principle. An external three-model review (ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, 2026-05-29) independently converged on retiring the mandate with high confidence; that convergence corroborates the derivation but the derivation, not the model count, is the proof.
alternatives_considered: Keep the mandate as aspirational only (rejected — even as aspiration it distorts candidate selection; the math forbids it, so it isn't aspiration, it's fiction)
Lower the mandate to a still-ambitious number like 50% (rejected — 50% CAGR requires Sharpe well above 2.0 under the 1.5% cap; same category of impossibility)
